summary:
# NOTES: Captain Kettle on the War-Path (C. J. Cutcliffe Hyne, Methuen 1916, 3rd ed.; Gutenberg #78784)

Single book, ten stories (Chapters I–X). Frame: Captain Sir Owen Kettle K.C.B. (red torpedo beard, wooden leg, Wharfedale farm, wife Lady Kettle, daughter Mrs. Hunter, grandson Arthur Hunter, patent "Kettline"/Quale's Sheep Dip, Horner's Perfect Cure, preaches for Wharfedale Particular Methodists). Associate: Martin Carnforth, M.P. (grouse moor, Cow Ghyll butts, Coronas Colorados, butler Booker). Other recurring: McTodd (mahogany leg maker), Dr. Mary Brown (Norfolk, Wych Street, suffragette flag, leather breeches, "Call me Doctor"), Holly Holroyd (actor, "Jasper Kay" in "The Reptile"), Lady Kettle (business lady, bans female doctors).

## I. The Supply Ship
- Kettle at farm; Lady Kettle: wooden leg mahogany by McTodd; American limb £26 18s. Kettle's roses; "Kettline" mildew mixture.
- Carnforth recruits; target: German submarine off Ireland. Sailing from New Orleans (hotel under assumed names: "Mr. Martin" and "Colonel Owen").
- Tanker *Grüda* (Norwegian-owned, Chicago charter, 1,800 tons). Carnforth's failed bribe; runner Morrissey (saloon off Canal St., broken nose from Kettle). Drugged, shanghaied; Carnforth made stoker "Olsen", Kettle pantryman; mate's head banged on stanchion; mate named Schlich-like; "jury leg" stolen by Morrissey.
- Kettle's "wait and see" advice; loose belaying pins as weapons.
- German submarine (19 knots) moored to booms; 6 Germans; Whiteheads transhipped; 3 Germans killed by shell explosion, booted overboard; Norwegians forced to drink/dance; waltz on harmonium.
- Kettle throws Norwegian captain down ladder, knocks out quartermaster, Full speed ahead; rams submarine; torpedo tube fires; submarine explodes. *Grüda* sinks. Lifeboat of Norwegians shot by second submarine. Kettle and Carnforth right boat, reach Irish coast; Kettle sends wire about roses first.

## II. The Mine-layer
- Grimsby trawler *Grimsby Twins* (Captain John Henry Shepherd; twin sons John Henry and Arthur Cleethorpes Shepherd; cat Joe). Struck mine; twins killed. Shepherd prays for vengeance.
- Crew: McCrae (chief engineer, nephew Jimmy killed), Olssen (Third Hand, Germanic, killed later), old Dick (cook; son killed). Survivors take trawler *Bishop Argles* (Lowestoft, Tommy Argles murdered).
- Boarding of mine-layer; axe kills officer. Olssen killed overboard ("Deutschland uber alles"). Mines lifted; Shepherd's mine-laying plan.
- Mines fastened to otter boards, laid in Heligoland Bight; periscope pilots them through; cruiser (battle cruiser) rammed by *Bishop Argles* at mine; sunk.
- Epilogue: Shepherd lives; frame of 76 German helmet spikes; cat with one ear; newspaper: Berlin says British lost 13 destroyers.

## III. Cotton
- Holroyd (actor, former land-agent to Sir Berkeley Craig, Stock Exchange, chartered accountant) persuades Kettle: stop cotton to Germany. Kettle's "second-best leg."
- Fire-tabloids "fluxite" + "deferred ignitor"; air-gun darts. Journey to continental port (Ballahassee-named joke); hotel "Ambassadors' suite"; "Professor Owen". Big German with spectacles and upturned moustache (Kettle: "crossed-eyed son of dog") fights; roof escape; water tower; cotton bales fired; German (spectacled, upturned moustache) burned.
- Kettle wires Lady Kettle about curd cheesecakes for Arthur. Holroyd's dyewares option; "fifty thou'."

## IV. Gun-runners
- Captain Image (Black Funnel Co., *M'poso*, West Africa); Fourth Mate "Jones" (actually Navy: Lieutenant-type disguised as Jones, Welsh-named cover, Lee?) ; Purser Balgarnie; Third Mate Price.
- Abadah colony: Acting-Governor Crawford; Commandant Craigie of Hausa Constabulary (238 men). Schmaltz buys *Abadah Times and Echo*. Dr. Carl Josephs (butterflies, German agent), headman's Winchesters.
- Schmaltz cargo "S-in-a-ring-in-triangle" dumped; Gebruden (double-A-in-a-long-diamond) cargo of guns; Jones hooks Schmaltz, hoists him by winch.
- Epilogue: Crawford knighted after proclaiming protectorate; Lee-Wentworth (Gunnery-Lieutenant, *Desolation*), Josephs hanged on crucifixion tree.

## V. The Intervening Wire
- Dr. Mary Brown watches German submarine off Wales; Kettle's compass-deflection with wires; Brown's motorboat; oil from sunken marine boilers; Kettle captures submarine; hatch lashed; Ulfrida Crump trawler (13 crew) reveals; Kettle shoots; torpedo from bow tube via switch box; trawler sunk.
- Kettle wounded in forearm, Horner's Perfect Cure.

## VI. Rejoining at Once
- Lieutenant John B. Plough, R.N. (Marienbad; girl). Train to Port (Germany); arrested with Madame Arthur (Bradford millinery, "Manningham", "Madame Arthur. Modes et Robes"). Escape, stolen collier; Hula cruiser; Plough's fog-smoke trick; coal-boiler dropped on destroyer. Arrives Harwich.

## VII. The Lady Killer
- Kettle shoots sniper in grouse butt; sniper "Fräulein Berta Schauer" (pear-shaped, spectacles, moustache), Sir Hermann Vogelheimer (baronet, Carnforth's Party funds).
- Derelict barquentine gun-pit; German submarines; Carnforth knocked down by Kettle; submarine sunk by 3-inch shell; Kettle plays accordion ("As pants the hart"); destroyer; "Who hanged Sir Hermann Vogelheimer?"

## VIII. An Eye for an Eye
- Belgian war; Kettle rescues wounded soldier; staff subaltern (sapper, pipe); Joseph Mumm (humpback, cinematographer, drugs), Madame Mumm; mechanics' Lodge; boiler-vat traction engine escape to Holland; Madame killed; Joseph betrays; film of 23 hanged German officers.

## X. That Rhine Tour
- Kettle letter; Zeppelin captured on Yorkshire moor (adit prisoners); Dr. Brown stows away; Zeppelin's engine failure; drifts over Kiel Canal; Carnforth bombs; drifts to Denmark; Zeppelin burned; Kettle's Rhine poems.

## X (second) The Inventor of Meltite
- S.J. Livingstone (born Solomon Levenstein, Paisley; dyewares, Livingstone & Co., 29 Chapel Row, Bradford); invents Meltite (thermit-like). Sells to Sir Thomas Hillcote, seventh baronet, motorboat *Drowning Made Easy*, with ex-Lieutenant Bell (locomotor ataxy). Sinks ships with German disguise; Bell killed, Hillcote dies; Livingstone captured by Germans; refuses formula until earldom and £2m. Ends: "I wonder if they will succeed?"
